claims.text: Integrating metadynamics into dealloying or self-assembly will direct atomic diffusion along favorable pathways.
Metadynamics-guided dealloying or self-assembly will produce interconnected three-dimensional HEA nanoframeworks.
The resulting nanoframeworks will have superior atomic precision and complex, catalytically active surface structures.
Suitable starting materials are noble metal–based HEA precursors prepared as homogeneous solid solutions or nanoparticles.
Metadynamics can be used to map and exploit the free-energy landscape during a controlled dealloying or self-assembly synthesis.
Fine control of temperature, local composition gradients, and kinetic barriers during synthesis will improve framework formation.
Elevated temperature can activate pronounced atomic diffusion in noble metal–containing HEA nanoparticles.
The relevant application environments require high surface area and robust, atomically precise frameworks.
A free-energy landscape governs atomic diffusion and intermediate-structure formation during dealloying or self-assembly.
Metadynamics will reveal critical energetic intermediates and dominant diffusion pathways in the HEA synthesis process.
Controlling the identified pathways will direct atomic rearrangements into interconnected three-dimensional frameworks.
Framework self-assembly will create tailored defects and active sites for catalysis.
Atomic diffusion can drive structural and chemical evolution, including surface-layer formation and phase separation, in AuCoCuNiPt nanoparticles at high temperature.
The proposed process will yield greater atomic precision and surface complexity than conventional high-temperature processing.
Greater atomic precision and surface complexity will improve catalytic performance.
Traditional high-temperature alloying or dealloying typically produces bulk or poorly controlled surface architectures without atomic-level precision.
The proposed method will be effective only when relevant free-energy intermediates and kinetic barriers are accessible to metadynamics-guided control.
Extreme compositional complexity or excessively rapid atomic diffusion may reduce the method's utility.
The exact synthesis parameters and magnitude of catalytic improvement remain experimentally unvalidated.
